title: Tan... como: comparar poder y tamaño

sections.content: Tan + adjective + como (as... as) makes an equative comparison -- stating that two things are equal, or pointedly unequal, on some measure. It's the natural tool for sizing up the real power gap between the US and any single Latin American country, or its opposite, mutual need. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Ningún país latinoamericano llegó a ser tan poderoso económica y militarmente como Estados Unidos.
items.english: No Latin American country came to be as economically and militarily powerful as the United States.

items.spanish: Esta enorme asimetría de poder no era tan simple como una simple relación entre un país fuerte y varios países débiles.
items.english: This huge power asymmetry was not as simple as a mere relationship between one strong country and several weak ones.

items.spanish: Estados Unidos necesitaba los mercados, las materias primas y la estabilidad política de la región tanto como la región necesitaba su capital y su tecnología.
items.english: The United States needed the region's markets, raw materials and political stability as much as the region needed its capital and technology.

items.spanish: Esta relación profundamente desigual pero mutuamente necesaria definiría buena parte de la historia latinoamericana del siglo veinte.
items.english: This deeply unequal but mutually necessary relationship would define much of twentieth-century Latin American history.

sections.content: With a verb instead of an adjective, the pattern shifts slightly to tanto como (as much as) -- necesitaba... tanto como la región necesitaba..., not tan como -- so watch whether you're comparing a quality or an amount/action.
